name: Carlos Mendoza

five_sec.what_is_it: It plans dinners and texts the family to vote, then puts the list in Instacart or Walmart.
five_sec.trust_why: Walmart is right there and it says no card. But first thing it says is 'texts everyone in your house.' Why do they need everybody's number?
five_sec.next_step: Look for the price and the privacy part.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It says it in green: 'We don't deliver food.' OK, good, at least they say it.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Nothing on the page tells me what they do with my family's phone numbers. Only a 'Privacy' link at the very bottom. And every sample is 'family of 4'. We're seven, my suegra included.
full_page.whats_missing: A plain privacy promise next to the texting part. H-E-B (I'd use Walmart instead). Spanish. Food like what Rosa cooks, more than a taco night.

DD.quote: It wants to text everybody in my house, my suegra too. Where does it say what they do with our numbers? Just 'Privacy' at the bottom.

five_sec.what_is_it: An app that picks dinner for you.
five_sec.who_for: Moms with time to play with apps.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Trusted by 90,000+ families,' says who? And the big button is a letter from the CEO. I don't know this CEO.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: A phone with a bowl of rice and 'I've picked out meals for you.' Could be they send it, could be not.

full_page.what_stopped_me: The FAQ says their 'intelligence' writes the recipe. A computer making up food. And $25 a month on the pricing page.
full_page.whats_missing: Real recipes from real people. A price I can afford for seven.

OL.quote: 'Ollie's state-of-the-art intelligence... writes a recipe just for you.' So a computer is making up the food. Rosa would laugh at me.

five_sec.what_is_it: App for saving recipes and grocery lists.
five_sec.who_for: People who cook from the internet a lot.
five_sec.trust_why: The stars look good, 4.8. Says no card for the trial.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It's an app, the picture is a lady writing in a notebook.

full_page.what_stopped_me: I have to put my own recipes in. Marisol and Rosa cook from memory, not websites. And it's $5.95 a month after.
full_page.whats_missing: Something that plans for us. H-E-B or Walmart by name.

PTE.quote: I like that they say 'We never sell your data.' But I gotta bring my own recipes and type them in? Nobody in my house has time for that.

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal plans? A video with a mom and a little girl.
five_sec.trust_why: Looks like an old company. But a video tells me nothing.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Cartoon of a phone with food around it. Doesn't say yet.

full_page.what_stopped_me: A pop-up wanted my email for a 'special offer' and I scrolled to the end and never found a price.
full_page.whats_missing: The price. Whether they want a card for the 14 days.

EM.quote: 'More than two million customers,' OK. But no price anywhere, and a pop-up wants my email before I even know what it costs. What's the catch?

five_sec.trust_why: 'Open a box to reveal your offer.' Like a casino.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The green HelloFresh boxes on the screen. Everybody knows they send the box.

full_page.what_stopped_me: The pop-up asks for my email and my phone number to unlock the offer. And for seven people this would cost more than takeout.
full_page.whats_missing: A price without giving my zip code.

HF.quote: Open a box to win, then it wants my email and my phone number. For seven people? That's a car payment, mijo.

dd_offer.why: '14 days free, no card' I understand. But I still don't know: if I don't pay, do the texts to my kids keep coming, and does the free part really keep working?
dd_offer.expect_day_15: They ask me for the card. If I don't give it, I think the texting stops, but maybe the free part stops working too, or they keep messaging my family to get me to pay.

head_to_head.reason: It's free, it works with Walmart, there's a real mom who built it, and it doesn't push 'AI' at me.

OL.reason: No computer writing recipes, and free instead of $25.

PTE.reason: It plans for us; Plan to Eat wants us to bring the recipes and pay $5.95.

EM.reason: DinnerDrop shows the price ($0) and explains why it's free: Instacart pays them.

HF.reason: A grocery list for seven at Walmart prices, not boxes they won't even price without my zip code.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page hero and the Family section: right next to 'texts everyone in your house,' one plain line: 'We only use their numbers to send the dinner vote. We never sell or share them. Anyone can reply STOP.' And offer the texts in Spanish.
